change.title: pr-40940-flat
change.description: Fix concurrent group access to prevent NullPointerException
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Reader thread is never joined and is not stopped if a delete fails
findings.body:
The reader thread is started with no `join()`, and `deletedAll.set(true)` at line 155 is not in a `finally`. Two problems follow.

1. If any `remove()` at line 153 throws, `deletedAll` is never set. The thread then loops forever against the server and outlives the test.
2. On the success path, `assertThat(caughtExceptions, empty())` at line 157 runs without waiting for the thread's last in-flight `groups(...)` call. An exception from that call is added after the assertion and is lost. This is the final read, which is the one most likely to see an already-deleted group.

Fix: wrap the deletes in `try/finally` that sets `deletedAll`, keep the `Thread` reference, `join()` it with a timeout, and only then assert.

findings.title: Test does not assert that any read overlapped the deletes
findings.body: The test passes if the reader thread never completes a call while groups are being deleted. A count of successful or attempted reads, asserted to be above 0 and ideally started before the first delete, would show that the race was exercised. `groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)` uses the default `subGroupsCount=true`, so the path `GroupsResource.getGroups` → `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount` → `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount` is hit. The test should say what it targets. It currently has no comment or assertion tying it to the NPE in `getSubGroupsCount`.

findings.title: Only getSubGroupsCount is made null-safe; the sibling delegations still NPE on a deleted group
findings.body: `getSubGroupsStream(search, ...)` (lines 256, 262, 268) calls `modelSupplier.get().…` directly. `modelSupplier` wraps `getGroupModel()`, which returns null once the group is deleted, so these calls throw the same NPE under the same race. `getSubGroupsCount` now returns `null` in that case, so the REST representation silently omits `subGroupCount` instead of failing. `GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount` returns `Long`, but the JPA implementation (model/jpa/.../GroupAdapter.java:190) always returns a value. Decide whether a vanished group should be skipped by the caller, as `GroupUtils.populateGroupHierarchyFromSubGroups` could do, or handled consistently in the adapter. The PR body says it fixes concurrent group access to prevent an NPE, but only this one method is covered.

findings.title: Stray whitespace-only line and misspelled variable name
findings.body: Line 117 holds trailing spaces. `groupUuuids` has three u's. Line 145 is an empty line at the start of the catch block.

contracts.action: GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount now returns null instead of throwing NPE when the backing group no longer exists
contracts.equivalent_path: Sibling delegations in the same class (getSubGroupsStream overloads at lines 254-269) call modelSupplier.get() and dereference it unchecked. getDelegateForUpdate (line 57) throws IllegalStateException when the group is missing.
contracts.before_after: Before: getGroupModel().getSubGroupsCount() NPEs when getGroupById returns null (group deleted concurrently). After: modelSupplier.get() is null-checked and null is returned.
contracts.visible_effect: GET /groups with subGroupsCount=true no longer fails with 500 for a group deleted mid-request. The representation gets subGroupCount=null, which is omitted from the JSON, for that group. GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount (line 90) passes the null straight to setSubGroupCount(Long).
contracts.failure_mode: If the group is deleted between cache lookup and the count, the entry is still listed, with a missing count. The other sibling methods can still NPE.

summary: The `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount` null guard is correct and narrow. The `@Override` on `CachedGroup.getRealm` and the removal of the unused private method in `GroupUtils` are harmless. The new concurrency test has two real defects. The reader thread is never joined, so the final assertion can miss exceptions, and a failed delete leaves it spinning forever. The test also doesn't prove that any read overlapped the deletes. The sibling `getSubGroupsStream` delegations in `GroupAdapter` still dereference a possibly-null supplier result.
